title: Review (Supported): on fresh seeds 5 and 6, stopping the regrowth of r kills every neural-field comet within ~200 t, a cut in one half kills only that half's comets, and fed twins keep 37-40 dividing, travelling comets
summary: labkit runs of the claimed world on seeds 5 and 6, fed and forked at t=500 (cut_t=500 everywhere, and cut_half=1). Fed: 37/40 comets at t=1000 from full-domain noise, 106/111 tracks travel >= 1 body length (max 27/42 body lengths), 10/11 persistent splits, max generation 2/3. Cut everywhere: comets in each half fall from 15/22 (seed 5) and 13/20 (seed 6) to 0 by t~620-750; labkit 0 components at the end. Cut in the left half: left half 15/13 -> 0 by t~700, right half keeps 11/9 at t=1000 against 22/19 in the fed twin (c20's forkcount.py; forkcount_s5.png, forkcount_s6.png).

observations.S: rerun/fed/seed5/sheet.png t=0: noise over the whole domain
observations.M: rerun/fed/seed6/FACTS.md: 111 tracks >= 1 body length, max 42.1 body lengths
observations.E: forkcount_s5.png, forkcount_s6.png: cut everywhere -> 0 comets in both halves; cut left -> 0 left, 11/9 right vs 22/19 fed
observations.D: rerun/fed/seed5-6/FACTS.md: 10/11 persistent splits, max generation 2/3 from noise

controls_run.E: rerun/cut_all/seed5-6 and rerun/cut_left/seed5-6 against rerun/fed/seed5-6 (identical until t=500)

verdicts.limitation: Persistent splits are 10-11 per run here vs 25-29 in the claim's packs (generation 2-3); D still passes from noise. The fed half also loses comets when the other half is cut (22 -> 11, 19 -> 9), presumably comets swimming into the cut half; the local-cut test is per half, not per individual. E holds by construction (activity consumes r); the forks show how fast.
